result.summary:
I recomputed Report D57-3 task 1 independently from p2_frames.csv, p2_cells_e1.csv, the pilot snapshot files and c_cells.csv, without running CC's d57 scripts or any simulation, and wrote nothing in the repo (the only __pycache__ there dates from Oct 15). Every check agrees with CC to <= 5e-8 relative, which is the rounding of CC's 8-digit csv:
(a) All 8 cells' e_rec, SE and sd agree, plus left/right, e_end, e_hold, lines_y_end, psi6, Z and c. The per-run e_rec agrees for 400 of 400 runs.
(b) The three-box slope at eta 0.72 is -3.4538706 +- 0.0863353, chi2 27.5255/1, scaled SE 0.4529558.
(c) The four-cell slope is -3.4539533 +- 0.0868403, chi2 37.1476/2, scaled SE 0.3742585.
(d) The two segment slopes are -4.145667 +- 0.162600 and -2.441831 +- 0.201327.
(e) The eta 0.78 slope through the two turned cells is -4.240248 +- 0.056284.
(f) c at e = 0 is 13.747825, 13.749933, 13.676585, 13.707677 and 21.863036 for the five lines in that order.
(g) The pilot's e is 4.55581% +- 0.00683% (34 record frames per run, no NaN, lines along y in 4 of 4 compartments), and its c is 15.958363.
The claim that the three 0.72 points are not on one line holds: chi2 is 27.53 for 1 dof (p 1.6e-7), driven mostly by the G2_pinturned point (18.8 of it). It survives the true-minimum (ODR) fit, a fit with c errors only, and a larger SE_e for point 1. One caveat: the two G1 cells at H 30 differ in e by 7.7 SE while their c agree, so the slope's central value depends on how the combined point's SE_e is set. Scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chrisharing-Desktop-CCS-complex-coupled-systems-Repo-HardDisks/91cb08ec-0599-4faa-a6af-d5a7ca834255/scratchpad/d57a3/verify/v1_c_vs_e/: verify_c_vs_e.py, extra_checks.py, cmp_cells.csv, cmp_slopes.csv, my_runs.csv, run_stdout_v2.txt and extra_stdout.txt. verify_c_vs_e_v1.py and run_stdout.txt are the first run, which had a bool-sum bug in my own lines_y count; it is fixed in v2.

result.summary:
I recomputed task 2 of Report D57-3 (the bistable run: eta 0.78, G2, pin 0, M 1800, run 9) from the merged P2 tables with my own code, without running CC's d57 scripts or any simulation. Every number checked agrees with CC's bistable.md, bistable_runs.csv and bistable_scan.csv, to within the 8-significant-figure rounding of the CSVs (at most 2e-8 relative).

(a) Run 9's per-trajectory c is 26.692247; the siblings' median is 24.160484 (23.148171 to 24.733437). The +10.5 % excess comes almost entirely from nu_d (+4.97 sibling sd), not from tau_r. None of the 10 per-run fits is a stall.

(b) Run 9's record-mean strain is +2.0561 % left and -2.1364 % right; the siblings' right range is -2.557 to -2.127 %. Its strain at the hold's end is +2.301 / -2.643 % and at the end +1.936 / -1.544 %. Its record psi6 is 0.7456 / 0.7503 and its orientation minus pin +0.400 / -0.344 deg. I recomputed psi6 and orientation independently from the psi6_t file (circular mean over the record); all match.

(c) The (cell, M) E1 with all 10 runs is 24.309062 +- 0.310137 (tau_r 26.538, equal to KOA's acf_mean_fit.csv); without run 9 it is 24.041549 +- 0.175946. The without-run-9 value does not depend on which nu_ref is used (2e-9). No seed-averaged or jackknife fit stalled. As an extra check, the cell's E1 over the 5 masses is 23.8887 +- 0.0557 (chi2 7.21 / 4) with run 9 and 23.8897 +- 0.0504 (6.13 / 4) without.

(d) In the scan of all 800 compartments, only this one (run 9, left) lies more than 1 % from its cell-side median, at +13.29 thermal sd (thermal sd 0.328 %); the next largest is 1.32. The repository was not modified: helpers were imported with -B, and the __pycache__ mtimes are unchanged.
